name: ePayco

webhook.algorithm: FIELD-CONCATENATION HASH, not HMAC and not over the body. `x_signature` = SHA256 of six specific fields joined by the `^` character, in this exact order: p_cust_id_cliente ^ p_key ^ x_ref_payco ^ x_transaction_id ^ x_amount ^ x_currency_code. Plain SHA-256, no HMAC keying, NO timestamp — replay mitigation must be x_ref_payco dedup. A generator that hashes the raw JSON body will never match. Confirmation is also form-encoded, not JSON.

evidence.note: Catalog import from adversarially-checked research. The scheme above is quoted from that research and has NOT been transcribed into typed fields, so PagoKit will not generate a verifier. Promoting this provider to generic or build means reading the provider docs and typing the scheme in.

credentials.note: Uses P_CUST_ID_CLIENTE, P_KEY, PUBLIC_KEY and PRIVATE_KEY — four distinct values, no prefixes. The p_key participates in the signature itself. Does not fit the two-field key schema.

notes: The long-tail Colombian gateway with the broadest cash-network coverage and the lowest onboarding bar for individual sellers. Its signature scheme is the canonical example of a field-concatenation hash that never touches the request body — a pattern the generator currently cannot express.
SDKs: Official epayco libraries exist for PHP, Node, Python and Ruby (github.com/epayco), plus WooCommerce/PrestaShop plugins. Coverage is decent but the repos are aging.
Developer-experience scores are unrated placeholders (3/3); they are not used in ranking.
Overlaps: Third CO option after wompi and bold. Choose ePayco for cash-network breadth (efecty/baloto/su_red already in methods.json) and for individual sellers who fail Wompi's KYC.
Onboarding model was inferred during the catalog import and is not verified. Confirm it before relying on the "can this user actually get keys" filter.
